doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

title: Teaching improvisation at Mills and staying with an idea
summary: His improv class began with three-minute solos and duets explained to the class; he advises staying with a small idea until it reveals itself. Rowe quotes Karl Berger on freedom and precision.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Did you find that it helps that the audience have some information about your composing thoughts and why you made these choices?

Well you know I mean like I taught, you know, I mean well teaching at Mills College was the most time that I’ve ever taught at one place you know. And so I had a chance to develop all of these lessons and so on. For instance in my improv class the first class was always about everybody do a three minute improv and that way each student could hear, you know, what other people were doing, so the next assignment would be okay so select someone and come back next week and play a duet and be able to explain to the class

what you were working on. So if you don’t know what you was working on then you need to figure out how to get yourself to the point to where you can do that kind of thing and develop it. You know I mean and for me I mean the one easy way to do it is make sure you get to the bottom of the thought that you’re doing, you know, so you’re not just skipping over it. You know you want to stay with a small part of an idea until it starts to reveal itself to you. It’s similar to you know sometimes if I’m writing something and then there comes a moment where you know I’m not having to think about it anymore then I’m on the right path to developing it.

Very interesting. It makes me think a little bit about a quote I had a conversation with Karl Berger, the late Karl Berger. And he said — we were talking about sort of free jazz, and he said, “More freedom is not about less precision it’s about more precision. The more precise you get the more free you are. People think of a sense of freedom, free jazz, oh I can lose all the rules. I’m actually creating my own rules and they’re much more stringent.”
